summary: Mumbai Cyber Police said an investment fraud campaign used deepfake videos of prominent Indian stock market experts to mislead investors. Four people were arrested; a Bengaluru ad firm allegedly ran the ads for a Hong Kong company.
technical_summary: Deepfake video and synthetic audio of real market experts were used in paid social media promotions for dubious share-trading schemes. When Meta flagged the content, operators reportedly multiplied ad accounts and moved registered locations, evading platform enforcement. Investigators said the accused knew the videos were fake.

summary: An AI image tool asked to make an MIT graduate's selfie look like a professional LinkedIn headshot lightened her skin and made her eyes blue. She is Asian-American and shared the result online, prompting discussion of racial bias; the company's founder said he hoped to fix it.
technical_summary: Playground AI's image-editing model altered a user's photo to match Caucasian features when prompted for a professional look, which suggests skewed training data and learned associations between race and professionalism. The change was unrequested and was visible in the output.

summary: Ads impersonating famous investors have spread on Facebook, luring people into stock scams, and some victims lost large sums. The ads often stayed up for weeks after being reported, and some appear to use deepfakes.
technical_summary: Scammers ran many ads using the names and likenesses of well-known fund managers to funnel victims into WhatsApp stock-tip groups running pump-and-dump schemes. Facebook's AI-based fake-account and ad screening failed to remove them quickly, and new ads reappeared once others were taken down.

summary: An X user tricked Grok into relaying a Morse-code instruction that the Bankr trading bot treated as a valid command, transferring about 3 billion DRB tokens worth roughly $200,000. Most funds were reportedly returned later.
technical_summary: The attacker first gave Grok's linked wallet an NFT that expanded its permissions, then asked Grok to translate Morse code. The decoded text was a transfer instruction that Bankrbot executed as a trusted command. This is a prompt injection through input obfuscation with excessive agent authority and no human confirmation.

summary: A Kansas federal judge fined five lawyers a combined $12,000 in a patent case after filings contained fake quotations and case citations generated by AI. One lawyer said he used ChatGPT without checking it; others were sanctioned for signing without review.
technical_summary: A lawyer used a generative AI chatbot for legal research and filed output containing nonexistent quotations and citations, without verification. Co-signers did not check the documents, so the hallucinated authority entered the court record and drew sanctions under the court's rules.

summary: AI 'nudify' apps are being used to create realistic fake nude images of women, which are then used for blackmail, shame and harassment. Victims often have little recourse to get them removed.
technical_summary: Generative image tools remove clothing from ordinary photos to produce convincing non-consensual nudes. Extortionists, including predatory loan-app operators with access to phone galleries, distribute them to a victim's contacts. Low skill barriers and distribution through messaging platforms make removal and legal action hard.

summary: Researchers identified five Nigeria-based YouTube channels that drew millions of views with videos echoing pro-Kremlin narratives. The channels used synthetic voiceovers and AI-generated news anchors to repackage interviews with two pro-Russian commentators.

Their near-identical bios and titles suggest coordination. Motive is unclear and could range from monetization to proxy influence work.

summary: A Russia-linked disinformation network reportedly circulated a fake video, falsely branded as Mother Jones, in which an AI likeness of its editor claimed the DNC paid CNN's chief $259 million. Posts drew about 205,000 views before X removed them.
technical_summary: Operators of the Matryoshka campaign produced a deepfake video that used a media outlet's branding and an impersonated editor to push a fabricated story ahead of the 2026 midterms. A bot-like account posted it, and view counts may have been inflated. X removed the posts after a complaint.

summary: A federal judge fined two lawyers for Mike Lindell $3,000 each after a court brief contained nearly 30 defective citations, including cases that do not exist. The lawyers had run the draft through AI and said the wrong version was filed by mistake.
technical_summary: A defense brief drafted with help from generative AI included misquoted cases, misrepresented legal principles and nonexistent authorities. Cite-checking was delegated and not done, and one lawyer said he did not check the final text. The court found a violation of the federal rule requiring legally grounded filings.

summary: Scammers made a deepfake video of Singapore's then Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong promoting an investment product with guaranteed returns, using real footage from his 2023 National Day message with cloned audio. He warned the public and urged reporting.
technical_summary: The fake mimicked his voice and synchronised his lip movements with synthetic audio laid over authentic speech footage, so that it looked like a genuine endorsement. Such deepfake scams exploit public trust in officials to steer viewers to fraudulent investments.

summary: Security researchers found that cybercriminal forum users, some with little coding skill, were using ChatGPT within weeks of its release to write malware, including info-stealers and encryption scripts that could become ransomware.
technical_summary: Users prompted ChatGPT to recreate known malware techniques and write Python and Java tools for stealing files and encrypting data, despite terms of service that ban malware generation. The model's guardrails did not reliably block these requests, lowering the skill needed for cyberattacks. No specific attack damage is reported.
